name: The Bowne House
ctx: A Queens farmhouse of 1661 that became a birthplace of American religious freedom.

name: St. Paul's Chapel
ctx: Built in 1766, Manhattan's oldest surviving public building, and a survivor of the 1776 Great Fire and of 9/11.

name: Federal Hall
ctx: The epicentre of early American democracy and the site of George Washington's first inauguration.

name: City Hall
addr: City Hall Park, Centre Street, Manhattan
ctx: Completed in 1812, the oldest continuously operating city hall in the nation.
landmark: African Burial Ground & The Commons Historic District

name: Domino Sugar Refinery
ctx: An industrial icon on the Brooklyn waterfront that once processed most of the sugar consumed in America.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: Tweed Courthouse
ctx: A monument to nineteenth-century political corruption and the Tammany Hall machine.
landmark: African Burial Ground & The Commons Historic District

name: The Marble Palace
ctx: Built as the nation's first department store, transforming American retail. Later the Sun Building.
landmark: African Burial Ground & The Commons Historic District

name: 21 Stuyvesant Street
ctx: An early 1800s federal-style townhouse tied to Peter Stuyvesant's descendants.

name: The High Bridge
addr: Highbridge Park, Amsterdam Avenue and West 172 Street, Manhattan
ctx: The city's oldest standing bridge, built to carry the Croton Aqueduct across the Harlem River.

name: 123 Lexington Avenue
ctx: The brownstone where Chester A. Arthur was sworn in as President in 1881.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: Pier A
ctx: A harbour landmark and police station at Battery Park, a maritime gateway to the city.

name: The IRT Powerhouse
ctx: The Romanesque powerhouse built to generate electricity for the original subway lines.

name: The Bossert Hotel
ctx: The Waldorf-Astoria of Brooklyn, and the site of the Dodgers' 1955 World Series celebration.

name: The Asch Building
ctx: Site of the 1911 Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire, which catalysed nationwide labour reform. Now NYU's Brown Building.

name: The Flatiron Building
ctx: A pioneering triangular skyscraper that redefined the Midtown skyline.

name: The Lyceum Theatre
ctx: Broadway's oldest continuously operating legitimate theatre.

name: Sixty-ninth Regiment Armory
ctx: The armoury that hosted the 1913 Armory Show, introducing Americans to modern art.

name: The American Bank Note Plant
ctx: A fortified South Bronx plant built to print currency, stocks and stamps.

name: Grand Central Terminal
ctx: A Beaux-Arts civic monument that rescued Midtown and redefined public space.

name: The Apollo Theater
ctx: Harlem's cultural epicentre and a crucible for African American music and performance.

name: The Coney Island Boardwalk
ctx: A public walkway that democratised summer leisure for working-class New Yorkers.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: Bank of United States
ctx: The branch bank whose December 1930 collapse ruined thousands of immigrant depositors.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: The Empire State Building
ctx: Built at record speed during the depths of the Depression.

name: The Hunter College Gymnasium
ctx: Where the United Nations Security Council first gathered on American soil in 1946. Now Lehman College.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: First Houses
ctx: The nation's first low-income public housing project.
landmark: East Village / Lower East Side Historic District

name: 134 East Sixtieth Street
ctx: A townhouse converted into a pioneering community centre for shelter and rehabilitation.
landmark: Not in an LPC historic district

name: 60 Hudson Street
ctx: An Art Deco fortress built for telegraphy, later one of the most critical internet hubs on Earth.

name: Brooklyn Borough Hall
ctx: Brooklyn’s city hall until consolidation in 1898, and still the seat of the borough presidency.
